payload.headline: NVIDIA: CEO exit confirmed before earnings; strong business at a low-end price

summary.thesis: The business is growing faster and earning more cash than a year ago, and the price sits near the low end of fair value; the open questions are leadership and the earnings report on 2026-11-17.
summary.decision: Long-term hold, with no new money before earnings; no swing trade until the report is out.

payload.happening: NVIDIA closed at 173.73, up 2.87% on the day. An intraday reading of 164.74 (not a close) puts the stock inside its only support zone of 162.81–164.98. NVIDIA announced a CEO transition, and an 8-K filing confirms a change in its officers. Earnings arrive on 2026-11-17, and options are pricing a 9.9% move by the 2026-11-20 expiry.
payload.business: The numbers in the latest quarter (ended 2026-07-26) show a business that is speeding up, not slowing down. Sales growth versus a year earlier rose from 73.21% two quarters ago to 105.85%. Trailing revenue is 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, is 127.0B, up from 72.0B, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. None of that is changed by this week's news. The CEO transition and a board probe of Jensen Huang (reported; the company hired an outside prosecutor to lead it, reported) are governance events. They change sentiment now. They could affect strategy and key customer relationships later (general knowledge), but nothing in DATA shows that yet. The real business risks are elsewhere. Unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. A 65% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. Insiders also sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. Demand and cash are not at risk on today's data. Margins and the quality of receivables are the parts to watch.

worth.text: On earnings, the stock trades at 21.9 times the last year and 10.9 times next year's analyst estimate. On sales it trades at 13.8 times, below the peer median of 17.1 and at the 9th percentile of its own 5-year history. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values future cash in today's money) gives 195.92 / 228.42 / 272.22 for bear, base and bull. The price-to-sales history method gives 217.35 to 411.04. The DCF caps starting growth at 30%, so the gap between bear and bull comes mainly from the discount rate (9.9%, plus or minus 1 point). The bigger gap, between the DCF and the history method, comes from assuming the stock earns its past sales multiples again. Today's price implies free cash flow growth of about 22.7% to start, then fading. At 20% starting growth the value is 156.62; at 30% it is 228.42. The real swing factor is margin. If operating margin fell to 48%, the value drops to 117.71. My range is 156.62 to 228.42, and the price sits in the lower half of it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65%, not back toward 48%.

bull: Cheap against peers and its own past: price-to-sales of 13.8 compares with a peer median of 17.1 and sits at the 9th percentile of its 5-year range.
Growth is speeding up: quarterly sales growth went from 73.21% to 105.85%, and free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B.
Analysts' next-year EPS estimate of 15.91 rose 23.9% over 90 days, which puts the stock at 10.9 times next year's earnings.
bear: Margins may be at a peak: operating margin of 65% is the top of its 5-year range, and at a 48% margin the model value falls to 117.71.
Receivables grew 127% against sales growth of 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward.
The chart is weak: the price is in a downtrend below its falling 50-day average of 217.1, while the CEO changes and a probe (reported) run into earnings.

levels.what: Today's close, in the lower half of the 156.62–228.42 fair-value range; enough to hold, not urgent enough to add before earnings.
Bottom of the only support zone (162.81–164.98); an area to add after earnings if the margin and receivables data hold up.
Base-case DCF value; near here the valuation upside is used up and it is time to reassess.

longterm.why: The automated rule says buy and the committee says hold. With a confirmed CEO change, a reported probe and earnings days away, holding respects both a strong business and a cloudy near term.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend, with resistance at 175.15–179.53 (4 touches) sitting just above the close. Earnings fall inside the window, and the 9.9% implied move against an ATR (average daily range) of 8.7 means a report can gap straight through any stop.

decision.timing: Wait for the 2026-11-17 report. Option prices show implied volatility of 74.4 against 52.8 realized, so a big move is expected. Act after the report shows whether margins and receivables hold.

change_mind: Bearish: a close below 162.81 (support breaks), or an earnings report showing operating margin falling back toward 58.09% or below.
Bearish: analysts cut the next-year EPS estimate of 15.91, or receivables keep growing faster than sales.
Bullish: a close above 185.22 (top of the upper resistance zone) would break the pattern of lower highs and support adding toward 195.92.
